Fix a field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, an integer $d\ge2$, and positive integers $n_1,\ldots,n_d$. A finite order-$d$ tensor of shape $(n_1,\ldots,n_d)$ is an array $A=(A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d})$ indexed by $1\le i_k\le n_k$. Its Frobenius inner product and norm are
$$ \langle A,B\rangle_F=\sum_{i_1=1}^{n_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{n_d}\overline{A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}B_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}, \qquad \|A\|_F=\sqrt{\langle A,A\rangle_F}. $$
For a matrix, rank means the dimension of its column image and the Frobenius inner product is the same entrywise formula. The adjoint $M^*$ is conjugate transpose (transpose over $\mathbb R$).

For $1\le k\le d$, the mode-$k$ unfolding $A_{(k)}$ has $n_k$ rows and $\prod_{j\ne k}n_j$ columns. Its row index is $i_k$ and its column index is the remaining tuple in increasing mode order, lexicographically ordered. Its entry at that row and column is the corresponding entry of $A$. For $1\le k<d$, the cut-$k$ unfolding $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ has row tuple $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and column tuple $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, each lexicographically ordered. These conventions fix all reshapes used below.

derivations.claim: For a mode-$k$ unfolding, the map from a multi-index $(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ to the matrix position consisting of row $i_k$ and the ordered tuple of all other indices is a bijection: the row and column tuple recover every original index exactly once. Thus the entrywise sum defining $\langle A_{(k)},B_{(k)}\rangle_F$ is precisely the same finite sum as $\langle A,B\rangle_F$.

For a cut-$k$ unfolding, splitting the tuple into $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$ is also a bijection with the original multi-index set. Its entrywise inner-product sum therefore equals $\langle A,B\rangle_F$ as well. Taking $B=A$ and nonnegative square roots proves each norm identity.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

derivations.claim: Choose the full output singular-vector basis $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ from an SVD of $A$, ordered so its first $q$ vectors correspond to the positive singular values in the statement. The SVD sends each positive input singular vector to a nonzero multiple of its corresponding output vector and sends every remaining input basis vector to zero. Thus the image of $A$ is exactly $\operatorname{span}(u_1,\ldots,u_q)$, so $q=\operatorname{rank}(A)$ by [F1]. If $k\ge q$, then $A_k=A$ and $\delta_k=0$, so the lower bound follows from nonnegativity of the norm. Suppose henceforth that $k<q$, and let $B$ have rank at most $k$. Its column image has an orthonormal basis; let $P$ be the orthogonal projection onto that image. Then $PB=B$, and the columnwise orthogonal decomposition by $P$ and $I-P$ gives $\|A-B\|_F^2\ge\|(I-P)(A-B)\|_F^2=\|(I-P)A\|_F^2$.

Put $a_j=\|Pu_j\|^2$ for $1\le j\le q$. Since $P$ is an orthogonal projection, $0\le a_j\le1$. Expanding the SVD of $A$ and using orthonormality of $(v_j)$ gives $\|(I-P)A\|_F^2=\sum_{j=1}^q\sigma_j^2(1-a_j)$. If $(w_\ell)_{\ell=1}^{s}$ is an orthonormal basis of the range of $P$, then the full output basis from step 1.1 gives $\sum_{j=1}^q a_j\le\sum_{\ell=1}^{s}\sum_{j=1}^{m}|\langle w_\ell,u_j\rangle|^2=s=\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k$.

Write $\lambda_j=\sigma_j^2$, so $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_q>0$. Using $\sum_j a_j\le k$, $0\le a_j\le1$, and $k<q$, we obtain $\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_j a_j\le\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j a_j+\lambda_{k+1}\sum_{j=k+1}^q a_j\le k\lambda_{k+1}+\sum_{j=1}^k(\lambda_j-\lambda_{k+1})a_j\le\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j$. Therefore step 2.1 implies $\|A-B\|_F^2\ge\sum_{j=k+1}^q\sigma_j^2=\delta_k^2$.

The image of $A_k$ is contained in $\operatorname{span}(u_1,\ldots,u_{\min(k,q)})$, so its rank is at most $k$. The omitted SVD terms are pairwise Frobenius-orthogonal rank-one matrices because both singular-vector families are orthonormal; hence $\|A-A_k\|_F^2=\sum_{j=k+1}^q\sigma_j^2=\delta_k^2$. Together with step 3.1, this proves the truncation is optimal.

derivations.claim: The Gram matrix $G=M^*M$ is invertible: if $Gx=0$, then $0=x^*Gx=\|Mx\|_2^2$, so $Mx=0$; full column rank forces $x=0$. Thus the square map $G:\mathbb F^r\to\mathbb F^r$ is injective and therefore bijective in finite dimension. Define $W_*=G^{-1}M^*Y$.

Set $R=Y-MW_*$. Then $M^*R=M^*Y-M^*MW_*=0$. For every $W$, write $Y-MW=R+M(W_*-W)$. The two summands are Frobenius-orthogonal because $M^*R=0$, so $\|Y-MW\|_F^2=\|R\|_F^2+\|M(W-W_*)\|_F^2\ge\|R\|_F^2$.
Equality in step 2.1 requires $M(W-W_*)=0$. Full column rank implies each column of $W-W_*$ is zero, hence $W=W_*$. Therefore $W_*$ is the unique minimizer.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$. A tensor-train (TT) representation consists of integers $r_0=r_d=1$, internal bond sizes $r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$, and cores
$$ G_k\in\mathbb F^{r_{k-1}\times n_k\times r_k}\quad(1\le k\le d) $$
such that
$$ A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d} =\sum_{\alpha_1=1}^{r_1}\cdots\sum_{\alpha_{d-1}=1}^{r_{d-1}} G_1(1,i_1,\alpha_1)G_2(\alpha_1,i_2,\alpha_2)\cdots G_d(\alpha_{d-1},i_d,1). $$
An empty bond index set gives an empty sum, hence the zero tensor; in particular, all internal bond sizes zero represent zero. A bond size $r_k$ is the storage dimension contracted between cores $k$ and $k+1$. The cut-$k$ unfolding groups modes $1,\ldots,k$ against $k+1,\ldots,d$ as fixed in [[def-finite-tensor-arrays-and-frobenius-inner-product]].

For an internal bond $k$, an invertible matrix $S\in\mathbb F^{r_k\times r_k}$ gives a gauge transformation by replacing the two adjacent cores with
$$ \widetilde G_k(\alpha,i,\beta)=\sum_{\gamma=1}^{r_k}G_k(\alpha,i,\gamma)S_{\gamma\beta}, \qquad \widetilde G_{k+1}(\beta,j,\eta)=\sum_{\gamma=1}^{r_k}(S^{-1})_{\beta\gamma}G_{k+1}(\gamma,j,\eta). $$
Their contraction is unchanged because $\sum_\beta S_{\gamma\beta}(S^{-1})_{\beta\gamma'}=\delta_{\gamma,\gamma'}$.

The left matricization of core $G_k$ has row index $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and column index $\alpha_k$. The core is left-isometric if this matrix $L_k$ satisfies $L_k^*L_k=I_{r_k}$. The right matricization has row index $\alpha_{k-1}$ and column index $(i_k,\alpha_k)$; the core is right-isometric if its matrix $R_k$ satisfies $R_kR_k^*=I_{r_{k-1}}$. A TT is in mixed canonical gauge about core $\ell$ when cores $k<\ell$ are left-isometric and cores $k>\ell$ are right-isometric.
For tensors $A,B$ of the same finite shape, every mode unfolding and every cut unfolding preserves the Frobenius inner product and norm.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, where $m,n\ge1$, have a singular value decomposition
$$ A=\sum_{j=1}^{q}\sigma_j u_jv_j^*,\qquad \sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_q>0, $$
where $q=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. For an integer $k\ge0$, put
$$ A_k=\sum_{j=1}^{\min(k,q)}\sigma_j u_jv_j^*, \qquad \delta_k^2=\sum_{j=k+1}^{q}\sigma_j^2 $$
with an empty sum equal to zero. Then $\operatorname{rank}(A_k)\le k$, $\|A-A_k\|_F=\delta_k$, and every matrix $B$ with $\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k$ satisfies $\|A-B\|_F\ge\delta_k$.

Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. The input is a tensor $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$, and exactly one of:

- rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$; or
- absolute tail tolerances $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{d-1}\in[0,\infty)$.

At cut $k$, flatten the current remainder with rows $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and columns $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, where $\alpha_0=1$, and compute an exact compact SVD $M_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$. Its positive singular values are ordered decreasingly as $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_s$. Under rank caps choose $q_k=\min(c_k,s)$. Under tolerances choose the least $q_k\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$ for which $\sum_{j>q_k}\sigma_j^2\le\tau_k^2$. This set is nonempty because $q_k=s$ gives tail zero. Record the discarded tail
$$ \delta_k=\left(\sum_{j>q_k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}. $$

Reshape the first $q_k$ columns of $U_k$ into core $G_k$ and reshape $\Sigma_{k,1:q_k}V_{k,1:q_k}^*$ as the next remainder. After cut $d-1$, reshape the remaining matrix as $G_d$. If $q_k=0$, the remainder has zero row dimension; all later ranks and tails are set to zero and the remaining cores are the corresponding empty zero arrays. Thus the zero tensor has all internal ranks zero, a cap zero returns the zero tensor, and a tolerance large enough to select $q_k=0$ does the same. The output is the TT core list and the cut tails $(\delta_k)$. Any SVD tie at a retained cutoff may be resolved by any orthonormal choice within the tied singular subspace.

Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. The input is a valid TT core list for a tensor of order $d\ge2$ and exactly one of rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$ or absolute tail tolerances $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{d-1}\in[0,\infty)$.

1. **Left orthogonalize without truncation.** For $k=1,\ldots,d-1$, reshape core $G_k$ into a matrix with rows $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and columns $\alpha_k$. Compute an exact compact SVD $M=U\Sigma V^*$, replace $G_k$ by the reshape of $U$, and absorb $\Sigma V^*$ into the next core along their common bond. Omitting zero singular directions is exact. The resulting cores $G_1,\ldots,G_{d-1}$ are left-isometric.

2. **Truncate from right to left.** For $k=d,d-1,\ldots,2$, reshape the current $G_k$ into a matrix $M_k$ with rows $\alpha_{k-1}$ and columns $(i_k,\alpha_k)$, and compute an exact compact SVD $M_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$. If its positive singular values are $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_s>0$, choose $q_{k-1}=\min(c_{k-1},s)$ for rank caps, or the least $q_{k-1}\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$ with $\sum_{j>q_{k-1}}\sigma_j^2\le\tau_{k-1}^2$ for tolerances. Record $\delta_{k-1}=(\sum_{j>q_{k-1}}\sigma_j^2)^{1/2}$. Replace $G_k$ by the reshape of the first $q_{k-1}$ rows of $V_k^*$ and absorb $U_{k,1:q}\Sigma_{k,1:q}$ into the previous core.

If $q_{k-1}=0$, the represented tensor becomes zero; set all remaining internal ranks to zero and their unperformed tails to zero. If the input represents zero, return the all-zero-rank representation and zero tails immediately. The output is the rounded core list and all recorded cut tails. No finite-precision error guarantee is part of this exact-arithmetic procedure.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

derivations.claim: Any TT representation with bond size $r_k$ factors the cut unfolding as $A^{\langle k\rangle}=L_kR_k$: the columns of $L_k$ are the contracted first $k$ cores indexed by the bond $\alpha_k$, and the rows of $R_k$ are the contracted remaining cores with that same bond index. This is a matrix product through an inner dimension $r_k$, so $\operatorname{rank}(A^{\langle k\rangle})\le r_k$.

For rounding, let $C_\ell$ be the contraction of cores $\ell+1,\ldots,d$, with row index the bond after core $\ell$ and column index the suffix $(i_{\ell+1},\ldots,i_d)$; the empty suffix gives $C_d=[1]$. Put $R_\ell=C_\ell^*$. Backward induction from $C_d$ shows $C_\ell C_\ell^*=I$: if $G_{\ell+1}^{(R)}$ is the right matricization of core $G_{\ell+1}$ and $C_{\ell+1}C_{\ell+1}^*=I$, then $C_\ell=G_{\ell+1}^{(R)}(I_{n_{\ell+1}}\otimes C_{\ell+1})$, so $C_\ell C_\ell^*=G_{\ell+1}^{(R)}(I_{n_{\ell+1}}\otimes C_{\ell+1}C_{\ell+1}^*)G_{\ell+1}^{(R)*}=G_{\ell+1}^{(R)}G_{\ell+1}^{(R)*}=I$ by right-isometry. Forward induction similarly gives orthonormal columns for each prefix interface: $L_0=[1]$ and $L_j=(L_{j-1}\otimes I_{n_j})G_j^{(L)}$. Since $L_{j-1}^*L_{j-1}=I$, $(L_{j-1}\otimes I_{n_j})^*(L_{j-1}\otimes I_{n_j})=I$, so $L_j^*L_j=G_j^{(L)*}G_j^{(L)}=I$. When the right-to-left sweep processes cut $k$, cores $1,\ldots,k$ still have that left gauge and cores $k+2,\ldots,d$ have the right gauge. The current cut unfolding is $L_kM_{k+1}J$, where $M_{k+1}$ is core $G_{k+1}$ reshaped with row index the incoming bond and column index $(i_{k+1},\alpha_{k+1})$, and $J=I_{n_{k+1}}\otimes R_{k+1}^*$. Since $R_{k+1}^*R_{k+1}=I$, $JJ^*=I$. The local SVD truncation replaces $M_{k+1}$ by $M_{k+1}V_qV_q^*$, where $V_q$ has the retained right singular vectors, so the full unfolding changes from $L_kM_{k+1}J$ to $L_kM_{k+1}V_qV_q^*J=(L_kM_{k+1}J)(J^*V_qV_q^*J)$. Since $JJ^*=I$ and $V_q^*V_q=I$, $J^*V_qV_q^*J$ is the orthogonal projection onto $T_k=\operatorname{ran}(J^*V_q)$, a subspace of the suffix modes $k+1,\ldots,d$. Thus the resulting tensor is the projection onto $S_k=\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_k}\otimes T_k$. With $E=M_{k+1}(I-V_qV_q^*)$, the global residual norm satisfies $\|L_kEJ\|_F^2=\operatorname{tr}(J^*E^*L_k^*L_kEJ)=\operatorname{tr}(E^*EJJ^*)=\|E\|_F^2=\delta_k^2$. At the next cut $k-1$, the right interface $R_k$ has orthonormal columns spanning $T_k$. Its local embedding is $I_{n_k}\otimes R_k$, so every newly retained suffix vector lies in $\operatorname{ran}(I_{n_k}\otimes R_k)=\mathbb F^{n_k}\otimes T_k$. Hence $S_{k-1}\subseteq S_k$.

In full-rank TT-SVD, set $Q_0=[1]$ and recursively $Q_k=(Q_{k-1}\otimes I_{n_k})U_k$ using the left singular vectors retained at cut $k$. Since $Q_{k-1}^*Q_{k-1}=I$ and $U_k^*U_k=I$, the columns of every $Q_k$ are orthonormal. Substituting each exact SVD of the current remainder into the preceding factorization gives $A^{\langle k\rangle}=Q_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$ for each cut. The retained singular values are all positive, so this factorization has rank $r_k$. By step 1.1 no exact TT can have a smaller bond, proving the full-rank characterization.

For TT-SVD, let $S_0=\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ and, after truncating cut $k$, let $S_k=\operatorname{ran}(Q_k)\otimes\mathbb F^{n_{k+1}\times\cdots\times n_d}$. The retained prefix matrices satisfy $\operatorname{ran}(Q_k)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}(Q_{k-1}\otimes I_{n_k})$, hence $S_k\subseteq S_{k-1}$. At step $k$, the current unfolding is $(Q_{k-1}\otimes I_{n_k})M_k$. If $U_q$ contains the retained left singular vectors, the new unfolding is $(Q_{k-1}\otimes I_{n_k})U_qU_q^*M_k$, the orthogonal projection of the current tensor onto $S_k$. The discarded matrix $M_k-U_qU_q^*M_k$ has squared Frobenius norm $\delta_k^2$ by [F3]; left multiplication by the isometry $Q_{k-1}\otimes I_{n_k}$ preserves that norm by direct expansion of the Frobenius inner product, equivalently [F2].

In either algorithm, let $A_0=A$ and let $A_j$ be the approximation after the $j$th truncation in execution order. By steps 3.1 and 1.2, each step is an orthogonal projection onto a retained subspace nested inside the preceding one. Therefore $e_j=A_{j-1}-A_j$ is orthogonal to every later increment, which lies in the retained subspace at step $j$. Telescoping gives $A-\widehat A=\sum_j e_j$, an orthogonal sum, and each $\|e_j\|_F$ is the recorded tail for that cut. Hence $\|A-\widehat A\|_F^2=\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\delta_k^2$. If a zero-rank truncation occurs, the output becomes zero and the unperformed tails are zero, so this same argument includes that branch. If no positive singular value is discarded, every $\delta_k=0$ and the output is exactly $A$.

$$ \langle A,B\rangle_F=\sum_{i_1=1}^{n_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{n_d}\overline{A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}B_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}, \qquad \|A\|_F=\sqrt{\langle A,A\rangle_F}. $$
For a matrix, rank means the dimension of its column image and the Frobenius inner product is the same entrywise formula. The adjoint $M^*$ is conjugate transpose (transpose over $\mathbb R$).

For $1\le k\le d$, the mode-$k$ unfolding $A_{(k)}$ has $n_k$ rows and $\prod_{j\ne k}n_j$ columns. Its row index is $i_k$ and its column index is the remaining tuple in increasing mode order, lexicographically ordered. Its entry at that row and column is the corresponding entry of $A$. For $1\le k<d$, the cut-$k$ unfolding $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ has row tuple $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and column tuple $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, each lexicographically ordered. These conventions fix all reshapes used below.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$. A tensor-train (TT) representation consists of integers $r_0=r_d=1$, internal bond sizes $r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$, and cores
$$ G_k\in\mathbb F^{r_{k-1}\times n_k\times r_k}\quad(1\le k\le d) $$
such that
$$ A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d} =\sum_{\alpha_1=1}^{r_1}\cdots\sum_{\alpha_{d-1}=1}^{r_{d-1}} G_1(1,i_1,\alpha_1)G_2(\alpha_1,i_2,\alpha_2)\cdots G_d(\alpha_{d-1},i_d,1). $$
An empty bond index set gives an empty sum, hence the zero tensor; in particular, all internal bond sizes zero represent zero. A bond size $r_k$ is the storage dimension contracted between cores $k$ and $k+1$. $$ \widehat A=\sum_{j=1}^{R}F_1(:,j)\otimes\cdots\otimes F_d(:,j) $$

$$ (Z_k)_{(i_\ell)_{\ell\ne k},j}=\prod_{\ell\ne k}(F_\ell)_{i_\ell,j}. $$

and replace $F_k$ by $Y^*$. The matrix $\overline{Z_k}$ has full column rank, so the minimizer is unique by [[lem-full-column-rank-matrix-least-squares-solution]]. $$ A=\sum_{q=1}^{R}a_q^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_q^{(d)},\qquad a_q^{(k)}\in\mathbb F^{n_k}. $$
The empty sum is zero, so the zero tensor has CP rank $0$. The coordinate expansion
$$ A=\sum_{i_1=1}^{n_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{n_d} A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}\,e_{i_1}^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_d}^{(d)} $$

Its first-mode slices are $W_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $W_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. They are linearly independent, and $\det(xW_1+yW_2)=-x^2$.

Suppose $W$ had a two-term expression $a\otimes b\otimes c+a'\otimes b'\otimes c'$. The first-mode slices being independent forces $a,a'$ to be independent. If $b,b'$ or $c,c'$ were dependent, every linear combination of the two slices would have matrix rank at most one, so its determinant would vanish identically, contrary to $\det(xW_1+yW_2)=-x^2$. Thus both pairs are independent. For any $x,y$, the pencil slice is $(xa_1+ya_2)bc^{\mathsf T}+(xa'_1+ya'_2)b'c'^{\mathsf T}$. Its determinant is a nonzero constant times $(xa_1+ya_2)(xa'_1+ya'_2)$. Independence of $a,a'$ makes the two linear factors nonproportional, so this determinant has two distinct zero lines; it cannot equal $-x^2$, which vanishes on the repeated line $x=0$. This contradiction proves $\operatorname{rank}_{CP}(W)>2$, hence it is exactly three.

For every $\varepsilon>0$, define $W_\varepsilon=\varepsilon^{-1}\bigl((e_1+\varepsilon e_2)^{\otimes3}-e_1^{\otimes3}\bigr)$. This is a difference of two elementary tensors, with the scalar absorbed into one factor, so its CP rank is at most two. Expanding gives $W_\varepsilon=W+\varepsilon(e_2\otimes e_2\otimes e_1+e_2\otimes e_1\otimes e_2+e_1\otimes e_2\otimes e_2)+\varepsilon^2e_2^{\otimes3}$, so $\|W_\varepsilon-W\|_F\to0$. For a matrix, rank means the dimension of its column image and the Frobenius inner product is the same entrywise formula. The adjoint $M^*$ is conjugate transpose (transpose over $\mathbb R$).

For $1\le k\le d$, the mode-$k$ unfolding $A_{(k)}$ has $n_k$ rows and $\prod_{j\ne k}n_j$ columns. Its row index is $i_k$ and its column index is the remaining tuple in increasing mode order, lexicographically ordered. Its entry at that row and column is the corresponding entry of $A$. For $1\le k<d$, the cut-$k$ unfolding $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ has row tuple $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and column tuple $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, each lexicographically ordered. Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. The input is a tensor $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$, and exactly one of:

- rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$; or
- absolute tail tolerances $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{d-1}\in[0,\infty)$.

At cut $k$, flatten the current remainder with rows $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and columns $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, where $\alpha_0=1$, and compute an exact compact SVD $M_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$. $$ \delta_k=\left(\sum_{j>q_k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}. $$

Reshape the first $q_k$ columns of $U_k$ into core $G_k$ and reshape $\Sigma_{k,1:q_k}V_{k,1:q_k}^*$ as the next remainder. After cut $d-1$, reshape the remaining matrix as $G_d$. Its rows are orthogonal with norms $\sqrt{10}$ and $2$, so the leading singular value is $\sqrt{10}$ and the first discarded tail is $\delta_1=2$. The retained left vector is $(1,0)^{\mathsf T}$, and the remainder $\Sigma_1V_1^*$ reshaped as a $2\times2$ matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

The second remainder has singular values $3$ and $1$, hence its rank-one truncation discards $\delta_2=1$ and returns the tensor $\widehat A=3e_1\otimes e_1\otimes e_1$.
